business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Sales of Maternity and Infant Care Commodities

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (parent investor jurisdiction; target WFOE is registered in mainland China)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: mainland China applies a civil law system with socialist market economy characteristics, while Hong Kong SAR applies common law; WFOE formation is governed by mainland PRC law with Hong Kong corporate documents as parent/investor evidence.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA)
Arrangement between the Mainland of China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income and the Prevention of Tax Evasion
PRC Foreign Investment Law (2019) and Special Administrative Measures (Negative List) for Foreign Investment Access

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2006, as amended); PBOC/SAMR Measures for Beneficial Owner Registration and Administration of Market Entities (Order No. 3, effective November 1, 2024); Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Registration Administration of Market Entities; Financial Institution Customer Due Diligence and Customer Identification Measures; PRC Criminal Law Articles 191 and 312.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Hong Kong investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hong Kong-origin documents for mainland WFOE registration: certified true copy by a China-Appointed Notary Public and onward transmission through China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited for notarial verification; this route is not an Apostille and not consular legalization because Hong Kong and mainland China are within one sovereign state. For an investor in an Apostille Contracting State outside China: issue the certificate, notarize if required, and obtain one Hague Apostille from the designated Competent Authority. For an investor in a non-Apostille State: notarize and then legalize through the competent PRC Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Current Status Certificate of the Hong Kong investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same protocol as the Certificate of Incorporation: China-Appointed Notary Public certification and China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited forwarding for use in mainland China; for a foreign parent in an Apostille Contracting State, obtain a single Apostille only; for a non-Apostille State, complete consular legalization by the PRC Embassy/Consulate. The two authentication methods are mutually exclusive and must not be applied in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing incorporation of the WFOE and Power of Attorney for the formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or sole director of the Hong Kong investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Board resolution must be certified as a true copy and signed before a qualified notary. For Hong Kong entities: China-Appointed Notary Public certification followed by China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited verification for mainland China. For entities in an Apostille state: notarize and then obtain a single Apostille from the state's Competent Authority. For entities in non-member states: notarize and then apply for consular legalization at the competent PRC consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives and are never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Hong Kong investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry (filed copy) or the investor company (certified true copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If issued by Hong Kong Companies Registry, use a certified true copy authenticated by a China-Appointed Notary Public and transmitted through China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited for mainland use; no Apostille or consular legalization applies within the same sovereign. For a parent in an Apostille Contracting State, attach the notarial certificate and add a single Apostille; for a parent in a non-member State, use consular legalization at the competent PRC mission. Apostille and consular legalization are independent channels; they must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming banking history, account standing, and source of funds of the Hong Kong investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank maintaining the investor company's bank account in Hong Kong or the investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-issued letter must be notarized by a notary public. For Hong Kong-origin letters: China-Appointed Notary Public certification and China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited verification; no Apostille/consular legalization. For foreign banks in Apostille Convention states: issue, notarize, add one Apostille and use directly. For foreign banks in non-member states: issue, notarize, then legalize at the PRC Embassy/Consulate. The Apostille path and consular path are mutually exclusive; never chain them.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All direct shareholders, indirect shareholders that ultimately own 25 percent or more, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and proposed legal representatives of the WFOE shall be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and non-SDN lists, UK HM Treasury consolidated list, EU restrictive measures, and PRC domestic sanction and terrorist organization lists. The screening must also cover politically exposed persons and their family members and close associates, adverse media, enforcement actions, AML/CFT violations, fraud, sanctions evasion, and reputational red flags relevant to maternity and infant product safety. Each person's identity must be independently verified through government-issued IDs, passports, corporate registry extracts, and notarized or legalized corporate records. Any match, ownership ambiguity, or unexplained source of funds requires enhanced due diligence, legal counsel escalation, and refusal to proceed if the risk cannot be mitigated. All screening results and decisions must be documented, dated, and retained for at least five years after the relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Registration and Pre-approval System, accessible through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and local Market Supervision Administration online service halls
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The enterprise name must be composed of Standard Chinese characters; a supplementary foreign-language name is permitted for cross-border e-commerce but the Chinese name is the controlling statutory name for all official filings, contracts, seals, invoices, and bank accounts. Transliteration of non-Chinese investor names must follow Mandarin pinyin phonetic conventions, preserve at least one distinctive and recognizable element, and avoid invented or misleading characters. The statutory four-tier naming structure is: [administrative division] + [distinctive trade name] + [industry or business characteristic] + [organization form]. The administrative division may be omitted only where the business is nationally recognized, subject to authorization, and the authority must be satisfied that the name is not misleading.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the market regulation authority rejects a proposed enterprise name, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application within 60 days of written notice or initiate administrative litigation within six months. The appeal must be filed in writing through the local SAMR acceptance window or online system, specify the rejected name, attach the written rejection notice, demonstrate that the proposed name is distinctive, lawful, and not misleading, and include evidence of legitimate interest such as trademark registration, prior use, or ministerial authorization if a sensitive token is involved. If the rejection is based solely on a prohibited token, the applicant should revise the name and re-file. The reviewing SAMR body must issue a written reconsideration decision within 30 working days; if the reconsideration fails, the applicant may appeal to the competent people's court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a mainland China WFOE engaged in online maternity and infant e-commerce, a mere virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding address is not acceptable to SAMR for business license issuance, to the State Taxation Administration for VAT and corporate income tax registration, to Customs for cross-border e-commerce exporter registration, or to banks for RMB and foreign currency account opening. The WFOE must maintain a fixed, inspectable physical office location in the registration city, evidenced by a certified lease contract, rent payment receipts, utility bills, landlord identity/property ownership proof, and a visible registered-office sign. A serviced office or co-working space with a dedicated desk, meeting room, signage right, and an executed service agreement may be accepted if the bank and tax authorities approve it, but mailbox-only premises will cause rejection at bank account opening and may trigger tax de-registration and loss of commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: Medium-High. A newly established WFOE in maternity and infant goods online retail has an estimated 35 percent probability of an unannounced registry or municipal tax inspection within the first 12 months, and the probability rises to 55 percent if the registered address is a serviced office without permanent staff or inventory activity. Inspection checklist: registered office sign matching the business license; original lease contract and rent invoices; actual desks, computers, filing cabinets, internet equipment, and corporate seals; at least one manager or employee present during business hours; statutory books and records; VAT invoice books and bank statements; e-commerce platform agreements and order-management system; maternity and infant product compliance records, including CCC certificates, quality inspection reports, and material-safety certificates; payroll and social insurance records; procurement orders, logistics contracts, and warehouse/sub-stock records for online sales.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2018 Amendment), Articles 23 to 30 on formation of limited liability companies, Articles 33, 34 and 37 on corporate governance and shareholder powers; PRC Foreign Investment Law (2019), Articles 2, 6, 29 and 30; Regulations on the Administration of Company Registration; PRC E-Commerce Law (2018), Article 15 on market entity registration obligations for online trading businesses.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Market Supervision Administration (MSA) at the municipal or district level where the registered office of the WFOE is located.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application Form for Establishment Registration of a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a PRC wholly foreign-owned enterprise engaged in online retail (ISIC 4791). The registered capital amount is fixed in the Articles of Association and must be fully subscribed by the sole shareholder. Paid-in capital may be contributed in accordance with the contribution schedule in the Articles, and there is no blocked escrow account requirement for this e-commerce business. Foreign exchange capital contributions must be reported to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) and deposited into a verified foreign currency capital account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN WFOE LTD

WHEREAS, CN WFOE LTD (the 'Company') is being established as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company under the laws of the People's Republic of China, with its sole shareholder being a company organized under the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; and

WHEREAS, the Board of Directors must approve the subscription of share capital, the selection of banking institutions, the adoption of the registered office, and the appointment of statutory officers before the Company can commence lawful operations.

NOW, THEREFORE, the Board of Directors, acting unanimously and pursuant to the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, the PRC Foreign Investment Law, and the Company's draft Articles of Association, hereby RESOLVES as follows:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The Board acknowledges that the registered capital of the Company is [AMOUNT] in Renminbi, fully subscribed by the sole shareholder. The Board approves the capital contribution schedule contained in the Articles of Association and authorizes the Managing Director to execute all subscription instruments, open a foreign currency capital account, and deposit the initial paid-in capital in compliance with SAFE registration rules.

2. BANKING AND PAYMENT AUTHORIZATION. The Board approves the opening of a basic deposit account, a general settlement account, and any foreign exchange accounts at [BANK NAME], a bank licensed by the People's Bank of China and authorized to conduct cross-border settlement. The Board authorizes the Managing Director and the Financial Officer to act as joint authorized signatories and to apply for online banking, payment gateway arrangements, and foreign exchange filings.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The Board adopts [ADDRESS] as the Company's registered office and principal place of business. The Board authorizes the incorporation agent to execute the lease, obtain the landlord's ownership documentation, and file the registered address with the Market Supervision Administration, tax authorities, and relevant municipal agencies.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Board appoints [NAME] as Managing Director and Legal Representative, [NAME] as Supervisor, and [NAME] as Financial Officer, each with the powers and duties required by PRC law and the Articles. The Board confirms that none of the appointees is disqualified under the Company Law.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorizes the Managing Director to make all post-incorporation filings, including tax registration, social insurance registration, electronic commerce filing, ICP filing, customs registration, and any other regulatory approvals necessary to conduct online retail of maternal and infant supplies, and to execute all documents ancillary thereto.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Board has executed these resolutions on [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Registration Name Approval and Business Scope Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (MSA) Enterprise Name Registration System, accessible through the SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online name reservation application for the proposed Chinese and English company names. The application must include the intended business scope covering online retail of maternity and infant care commodities, the identity of the Hong Kong Sar shareholder, and the proposed registered address. The responsible clerk will screen the name against prohibited terms and conflicting registered names. If the foreign investor's name or the word 'wholly foreign-owned' is used, supporting notarized corporate documents must be attached. Any name objection must be resolved before the formal registration dossier can proceed. The applicant should verify that the business scope does not touch the Foreign Investment Negative List; if it does, the scope must be revised or additional approval obtained.
required_dossiers: Completed enterprise name reservation application
Notarized and authenticated certificate of incorporation of the Hong Kong shareholder
Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate of the shareholder
List of proposed directors, supervisor and legal representative
Proposed registered address and evidence of lawful right to use the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, the applicant must resubmit within five working days with a revised name or bring a letter of consent from the conflicting enterprise. If the MSA suspends the application for a compliance review, the applicant should respond to the written query through the online portal and may voluntarily withdraw and resubmit the application without penalty. A final administrative rejection may be challenged by administrative reconsideration within sixty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Assembly of the Formation Dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong notary public for the Hong Kong shareholder's corporate documents, followed by the applicable Mainland-recognized authentication procedure for cross-border notarial certificates.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Hong Kong notary public to certify the corporate existence, board resolutions, shareholder register, directors' list and incumbency of the Hong Kong shareholder. The notarial certificate must then be submitted through the recognized Mainland authentication channel. In parallel, the incorporating counsel should draft the Articles of Association, the shareholder's resolution approving the WFOE, the appointment of the legal representative, the supervisor appointment form, and the lease agreement for the registered office. All documents must be reconciled with the approved name and business scope. The assembled dossier must be translated into Chinese by a qualified translator and the translations certified as true if required by the local MSA.
required_dossiers: Notarized and authenticated corporate records of the Hong Kong shareholder
Draft Articles of Association of the WFOE
Shareholder resolution approving the establishment of the WFOE
Appointment documents for legal representative, supervisor and financial officer
Lease agreement and landlord ownership certificate for the registered office
Certified Chinese translations of all non-Chinese corporate documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notarial certificate is defective or rejected by the local MSA, the notary must reissue the certificate and, if necessary, a revised authenticated text must be transmitted to the Mainland receiving authority. The applicant should maintain a bilingual index of the dossier and promptly cure any missing seals, signatures or translation stamps. If authentication is challenged, the applicant may separately obtain a certified true copy from the Hong Kong shareholder and resubmit within the prescribed correction period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Establishment Registration to the Market Supervision Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (MSA) corporate registration window or its official online enterprise registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete application package electronically or in person, including the approved name reservation, application form, Articles of Association, shareholder identity and notarized foreign investor documents, legal representative identification, supervisor appointment, and registered office lease. The legal representative must sign the application in person or through an electronic signature verified by a recognized CA certificate. The MSA will review the WFOE against the Foreign Investment Negative List, verify the business scope classification under ISIC 4791, and issue an electronic enterprise registration certificate. No official filing fee is charged. After the MSA issues the business license, the entity is deemed lawfully incorporated.
required_dossiers: Signed Application Form for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Enterprise
Articles of Association executed by the sole shareholder
Approved enterprise name reservation notice
Notarized and authenticated corporate documents of the Hong Kong shareholder
Identification documents of the legal representative, directors, supervisor and financial officer
Registered office lease agreement and ownership certificate
Consent and signature specimens of the appointed officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MSA issues a rectification notice, the applicant must cure the identified deficiencies within fifteen working days and resubmit. If the application is suspended because the business scope appears to touch a restricted industry, the applicant must remove the restricted item or obtain the relevant industry authority's approval. If the registration is rejected, the applicant may request a written reason and may seek administrative reconsideration or judicial review under PRC law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Registrations, Banking and Foreign Exchange Approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration (local tax service office), local Social Insurance Bureau, municipal statistics bureau, People's Bank of China-regulated bank of choice, and SAFE provincial office for foreign exchange registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the business license, the company must open a basic deposit account at a licensed bank and complete the tax registration information pooling with the local tax authority. The company must register its legal representative, financial officer and payroll records with the social insurance bureau and statistical office. The bank will assist in filing the account information with the People's Bank of China. For the Hong Kong shareholder's capital contribution and future distributions, the company must register with SAFE through the bank under the foreign exchange registration procedure for direct investment, including reporting the registered capital, paid-in capital and shareholder details. All post-incorporation filings should be completed before any online sales operations commence.
required_dossiers: Business license issued by the Market Supervision Administration
Seal registration certificate and company seal specimens
Identifications of legal representative and financial officer
Tax registration information form
Social insurance registration form
Bank account opening application and treasury management mandate
SAFE direct investment foreign exchange registration declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or SAFE queries the capital contribution source or corporate beneficial ownership, the company must provide a source-of-funds declaration, audited financial statements of the Hong Kong shareholder, and a notarized board resolution of the shareholder. If tax registration is delayed, the applicant can present the business license and unified social credit code to accelerate the process. Administrative penalties are avoidable by completing all registrations within the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) for ICP filing, local public security bureau for cyber filing, General Administration of Customs for cross-border e-commerce enterprise registration if exporting, and local market supervision authority for e-commerce operator information publication.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company's website or app domain under an ICP filing with MIIT through the licensed hosting provider. Obtain the public security cyber filing for the e-commerce platform or website. If the company sells goods exported from mainland China to Hong Kong or other cross-border markets, register as a cross-border e-commerce enterprise with Customs and obtain the necessary customs code. Publish the company's business registration information, location, after-sales terms and contact details on the online storefront in accordance with PRC E-Commerce Law Article 15. No separate operating license is required for pure online sales of maternal and infant supplies under ISIC 4791, but the company must comply with product quality, labelling and consumer protection rules for the categories sold.
required_dossiers: E-commerce operator information publication certificate
ICP filing authority and hosting service contract
Public security cyber filing certificate
Business license showing e-commerce business scope
Product supplier agreements for maternal and infant supplies
Cross-border e-commerce customs registration form, if applicable
Data protection and privacy policy compliant with PRC PIPL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ICP filing is rejected, revise the website content and business description to comply with MIIT requirements and resubmit through the hosting provider. If customs registration is queried, provide contracts with the overseas buyer and product compliance certificates. Failure to publish e-commerce operator information may be cured by immediate online publication followed by a written compliance declaration to the local MSA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity operates as a pure online retail business under ISIC 4791 and has no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility requiring an industrial license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no official operating or manufacturing permit is mandatory for online sales of maternity and infant care commodities; the company only needs the business license, ICP filing, e-commerce operator information publication, and, if exporting, cross-border e-commerce customs registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Ecology and Environment review is not triggered by ISIC 4791 online retail activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the operation is classified as digital/online retail and does not trigger a Full EIA Report, Environmental Registration, or any requirement under the EIA Classification and Administration List.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero direct industrial wastewater, volatile organic compound, or hazardous waste discharge is generated by the e-commerce operation; only ordinary municipal office waste and domestic sewage from leased office premises are produced, which must be managed under the building lease and municipal sewer system obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no factory, chemical warehouse, or assembly line exists, and therefore no Civil Defense fire permit or structural load inspection is mandated. If the company later adds a distribution warehouse under ISIC 5210, the operator must obtain a Fire Safety Inspection Certificate from the local Fire and Rescue Authority and complete workplace safety filing under the PRC Work Safety Law.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online electronic portal: Electronic Tax Administration (e-Taxation) platform at etax.chinatax.gov.cn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the WFOE with the Administration for Market Regulation and obtain the Business License bearing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), an 18-character alphanumeric code that constitutes the statutory taxpayer identification number (TIN) for corporate income tax and VAT. Step 2: Within 30 days after the Business License is issued, complete tax registration information confirmation through the STA e-Taxation platform or the competent tax service hall, submitting the USCC, registered address, business scope, legal representative and financial officer identity data, capitalization, and bank account details. Step 3: The STA validates the data and opens the enterprise tax registration master file; no separate paper TIN certificate is issued because the USCC is the TIN/VAT registration number. Step 4: Determine VAT taxpayer status (small-scale taxpayer or general VAT taxpayer) and apply for VAT digital invoice issuance rights through e-Taxation. Step 5: For a non-resident investor without a permanent establishment in China, no PRC TIN is required; the WFOE must withhold PRC corporate income tax and VAT on any China-source payments, and treaty relief must be evidenced by the investor home jurisdiction tax residence certificate. Step 6: If the WFOE undertakes exports, complete the export tax rebate (zero-rate) registration filing and link banking settlement records with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange export proceeds monitoring system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity-level taxation: China does not provide check-the-box pass-through elections for a limited liability WFOE, which is automatically taxed as a resident enterprise on worldwide income. For VAT, an eligible small-scale taxpayer may elect to register as a general VAT taxpayer before exceeding the threshold; once registered as a general VAT taxpayer, the status cannot be arbitrarily terminated.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: People's Republic of China Value-Added Tax (VAT), a single national consumption tax administered by the STA on the supply of goods and services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no turnover exemption from tax registration for a WFOE; the mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration threshold is CNY 5,000,000 of annual taxable turnover. Below CNY 5,000,000 the taxpayer qualifies as a small-scale VAT taxpayer; crossing the threshold makes general VAT taxpayer registration compulsory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT special invoices must be issued through the STA National Unified Electronic Invoice Service Platform as full-digital electronic invoices using the tax control UKey or an STA-certified system-to-system API. The e-invoice platform assigns a unique 20-digit invoice number, applies the taxpayer digital signature, and receives the invoice data in real time at issuance; no lawful VAT special invoice can be issued outside this digital fiscal clearance environment. Anti-fraud controls include automatic cross-matching of invoice data with VAT returns and customs/export records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods, including baby and maternity supplies, qualify for the 0% VAT zero-rating when the WFOE is a general VAT taxpayer registered for export tax rebates, the goods are actually exported from PRC customs territory under an approved customs export declaration, the export sales proceeds are received and repatriated through a designated foreign-exchange bank, and the export transaction is included in the STA export tax rebate declaration with matching customs, logistics, and payment data. Qualifying cross-border e-commerce retail export shipments may also use the consolidated export supervision model to obtain zero-rating; services exported to non-residents must fall within the statutory offshore service zero-rating catalogue.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) with customs declaration number
Bill of Lading (or air waybill for air cargo)
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank-issued foreign exchange collection certificate evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA export tax rebate audit cross-checks the customs export declaration, logistics documents, upstream VAT invoice chain, and bank foreign-exchange receipts. If any document is false, incomplete, or inconsistent, the zero-rating/refund is clawed back with daily late payment surcharge at 0.05% and, under Article 66 of the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law, a monetary penalty of one to five times the amount of the refund fraudulently obtained. Serious cases involving counterfeit documents or fictitious exports are referred for criminal liability for fraudulent export tax rebates, and the taxpayer may be downgraded to restricted foreign-exchange/customs supervision status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC) together with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: For the mainland China WFOE with a Hong Kong parent, the renminbi is not fully convertible under capital account rules. Current account transactions, including cross-border e-commerce sales proceeds and payments for goods and services under ISIC 4791, are generally convertible once the bank verifies the underlying trade documents, invoices, logistics records, and SAFE filing codes. Capital account flows remain tightly controlled. Inbound FDI registered capital injections from the Hong Kong shareholder must be routed through a designated SAFE-registered foreign exchange bank into a capital account facility, and the subsequent conversion of foreign currency into renminbi requires a capital account settlement declaration with the bank. Profit repatriation or dividend remittance to the Hong Kong parent is permissible only after the annual financial audit is completed, corporate income tax is settled, statutory reserves are allocated, and SAFE verification of the dividend resolution and audited financial statements is passed. The WFOE may hold foreign exchange in an operational current account, but no unfettered overseas conversion or offshore clearing is allowed. Stripe and PayPal can serve only as front-end merchant collection tools; the underlying funds must be routed back into the Chinese banking system through licensed commercial banks. The overall regime therefore allows trade-led convertibility but imposes strict documentary substance, reporting, and capital account filing burdens.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China has abolished mandatory surrender of export foreign exchange receipts. There is no fixed statutory conversion ratio. Export proceeds must be repatriated into the Chinese banking system within 180 calendar days after the export customs declaration, unless SAFE grants an extension. The WFOE may retain 100% of verified export foreign currency receipts in a designated foreign exchange current account or sell them to an authorized bank at the prevailing market rate. Conversion to renminbi is optional and must be supported by underlying trade documents, customs records, shipping bills, and e-commerce platform settlement statements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMIs, including neobanks and payment service providers, are not legally permitted to replace a licensed Chinese commercial bank as the treasury and FX clearing bank for a mainland WFOE. Such entities are not licensed by SAFE or the PBOC to operate renminbi corporate settlement accounts, execute capital account conversions, or provide foreign exchange verification for FDI flows. Stripe and PayPal may be used only as auxiliary merchant collection rails for low-value cross-border e-commerce sales; the collected funds must ultimately be channeled into the WFOE's domestic bank account through lawful trade settlement procedures. Any proposal to place primary corporate liquidity or FX execution with an offshore EMI is non-compliant and must be rejected.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence and in-branch KYC interview are mandatory. The statutory director and beneficial owners of the WFOE must appear in person before the commercial bank's compliance officer in mainland China for a face-to-face interview, original document verification, and biometric identity confirmation. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted for a WFOE corporate account. A notarized and legalized power of attorney may assist in routine signing authority once the directors and ultimate beneficial owners have completed the initial in-person onboarding, but it cannot substitute for the mandatory personal appearance requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity because the Hong Kong parent is a corporate shareholder and the natural-person ultimate owner is not immediately visible on the Chinese business license.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of the Hong Kong parent's Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate, NNC1/NAR1 annual returns, current shareholders register, directors register, ultimate beneficial ownership declaration, trust or nominee deed if applicable, and audited financial statements, together with copies of passports or national identity documents for every beneficial owner holding 25% or more, a notarized corporate group structure chart, and an up-to-date Companies Registry search report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction profile mismatch: high-frequency, low-value cross-border e-commerce receipts through Stripe and PayPal may appear inconsistent with the stated maternity and infant supplies business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete operational file including the WFOE's e-commerce platform merchant agreements, payment processor settlement statements, product catalog and pricing sheets, customs export declarations, freight and logistics bills, third-party warehouse inventory reports, refund and chargeback registers, and customer order data linked to ISIC 4791 online sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commingling of FDI capital account funds with current account sales revenue, creating a structural AML red flag and risking SAFE capital account violations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI registration certificate or after-filing receipt issued for the foreign exchange capital account, board resolution of the Hong Kong parent approving the equity injection, bank-source financial statements of the Hong Kong company, a fully itemized use-of-funds business plan, and an explicit board undertaking to maintain separate accounts for registered capital injection and operational revenue, with monthly reconciliation statements and no overdrafts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure or counterparty risk in the cross-border supply chain, including overseas buyers, freight forwarders, or payment intermediaries connected to restricted jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A counterparty due diligence pack containing signed contracts and invoices for all major suppliers and distributors, shipping and courier transaction manifests with vessel or airway details, completed sanctions screening questionnaire, negative media checks, OFAC/UN/EU/PRC sanctions screening results, export license confirmation from MOFCOM where applicable, and a written enterprise trade compliance policy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Hong Kong shareholder must remit the approved FDI registered capital via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's SAFE-registered capital escrow account held at a licensed Chinese bank. The wire must reference the SAFE FDI registration number and use the foreign exchange purpose code for inbound direct investment registered capital, typically recorded by the receiving bank under SAFE's capital project information system. Upon receipt, the bank issues an inbound foreign exchange payment notice and handles the capital account settlement into renminbi under the negative list. A Chinese certified public accountant is then engaged to issue a capital verification report, which is filed with SAMR and SAFE and serves as evidence of paid-in capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlements with domestic Chinese suppliers, the WFOE will clear renminbi payments through CNAPS or the RMB Core Clearing System. For cross-border trade settlements with overseas vendors and logistics providers, the permitted rails include SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers, irrevocable commercial letters of credit for bulk inventory purchases, and documentary collections where deferred payment terms are agreed. For cross-border renminbi trade settlements, CIPS can be used to reduce costs and improve traceability. All outbound payments must carry the correct SAFE trade purpose code and supporting commercial invoices, contracts, and transport documents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore plain-vanilla renminbi or foreign currency FX forwards executed with a SAFE-approved domestic bank, supported by underlying trade or capital flows.
Cross-currency swaps for intercompany funding and working capital hedges, limited to actual exposure and subject to bank counterparty and SAFE reporting approval.
Plain-vanilla FX options for hedging confirmed trade receivables; exotic derivative structures and speculative options are not permissible for the WFOE.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted onshore for the mainland WFOE; only the offshore Hong Kong treasury vehicle may access NDF markets outside mainland China.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form NAR1) under Companies Ordinance Cap. 622 s. 662
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary date of incorporation of the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers escalating penalty fees: USD 53.85 (late up to 3 months), USD 107.69 (3-6 months), USD 161.54 (6-9 months), USD 215.38 (over 9-12 months); failure to deliver the annual return for 12 months or more is an offence punishable by fine, and the Registrar may initiate strike-off of the company from the Companies Registry under Companies Ordinance Cap. 622 s. 744.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of expiry of the current certificate, as set out in the IRD's annual renewal reminder; late renewal is permitted for a 30-day grace period but carries an additional late fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew triggers a HK$300 late renewal fee; a business operating without a valid Business Registration Certificate is in contravention of the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), subject to prosecution, fines, and default assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) together with audited financial statements and tax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be filed within the date stated on the notice, generally one month after issue; professional block extension deadlines apply for accounts with financial year end in December/January/March months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The IRD will raise an estimated assessment under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) s. 59(3); default penalties under s. 80 and s. 82 include a fine of up to HK$10,000 plus 3 times the tax undercharged for deliberate conduct; a 10% additional assessment may also be imposed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form BIR56A) and Employee's Returns (Form BIR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the issue date, generally on or before 1 May, in respect of the salary period ended 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file renders the company liable to prosecution and to an estimated assessment of director's emoluments and employee remuneration; late-filing penalties apply under the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and adoption of audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external filing required; minutes to be kept in the Minute Book at the company's registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Unless dispensed under Companies Ordinance Cap. 622, the AGM must be held within 9 months after the end of the accounting reference period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors failing to call the AGM are liable to a fine and may be subject to court proceedings by members; failure to table audited financial statements at the AGM may also constitute a company law default affecting director eligibility and corporate standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Significant Controllers Register (SCR) annual confirmation and update protocol
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing required; register must be kept at the registered office and made available for inspection by the Companies Registry and law enforcement authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation: update the register within 7 calendar days of any change, including changes arising from shareholding transfers; no separate annual SCR return is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-maintenance or incomplete SCR is a continuing offence; the company and every responsible officer are liable to a fine at level 3 (HK$10,000) plus a daily default fine.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Hong Kong private company must appoint an independent Certified Public Accountant (CPA) auditor and prepare audited financial statements under Companies Ordinance Cap. 622 Part 9 unless it qualifies for the audit exemption under s. 359C as a small private company or small group. The quantitative exemption thresholds are: total annual revenue not exceeding HK$10,000,000, total assets not exceeding HK$10,000,000, and total employees not exceeding 100, with no group member being a listed company, bank, insurance company, licensed financial institution, or company engaged in regulated activity. Any company exceeding any of those limits, any group member exceeding those limits in aggregate, or any company whose shareholders elect not to use the exemption is subject to mandatory independent CPA audit. A dormant company may apply to the Registrar for exemption from preparing financial statements and from audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which are aligned with IFRS; eligible private entities may apply Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standard for Private Entities (HKFRS for Private Entities) or the HK SME Financial Reporting Standard if permitted by the HKICPA; all financial statements must comply with Companies Ordinance Cap. 622 and the Companies (Disclosure of Information) Regulations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Significant Controllers Register (SCR) is maintained at the registered office. There is no separate annual external confirmation filing to the Companies Registry for the SCR; however, Form NAR1 (Annual Return) serves as the annual confirmation of members, shares, changes in control, and registered office details. Any shareholding transfer or change in significant control (holding or controlling 25% or more of beneficial ownership/governance) must be recorded in the SCR within 7 calendar days and the Register of Members must be updated concurrently. For share transfer instruments, the instrument must be presented to the Collector of Stamp Revenue within 30 days of execution if executed in Hong Kong (or within 40 days if executed outside Hong Kong), with stamp duty payable at 0.1% of the consideration or net asset value per transfer (aggregate 0.2% for seller and buyer).
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Share Certificate Register and Instruments of Transfer

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - 2,500 per annum for registered office and corporate secretarial agent services in Hong Kong; typical mid-market range is USD 1,200 - 1,800
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 10,000 per annum for a cross-border e-commerce SME with a Hong Kong vehicle holding a WFOE, depending on transaction volume, group structure, and HKFRS/IFRS compliance requirements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard PRC Enterprise Income Tax rate is 25%; preferential 15% rate for qualified High-and-New-Technology Enterprises; small low-profit enterprises may benefit from an effective 5% levy (for taxable income up to RMB 3,000,000, an effective rate derived from a 20% reduced rate applied to a 25% taxable-income base under current MOF/SAT policy); eligible R&D expenditures may claim a 100% super-deduction; no general patent box exists in mainland China, and free-zone incentives such as Hainan Free Trade Port 15% rate apply only if the WFOE is specifically registered and engaged in encouraged activities there.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A100000), together with Quarterly/Provisional Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form A200000), filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal (e-Tax / Electronic Tax Bureau) and the Non-Resident Enterprise Income Tax withholding reporting module for outbound payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement return with quarterly provisional prepayment filings; quarterly reports are filed throughout the fiscal year, followed by an annual return and final settlement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional CIT prepayments are due within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter; the annual A100000 return and final tax settlement must be filed and fully paid on or before 31 May following the fiscal year-end (fiscal year is 1 January to 31 December).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from online retail sales of maternity and infant care commodities, including domestic e-commerce platform sales and cross-border online sales, stated before deduction of platform commissions and refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all China-source sales attributable to the WFOE even if payment is settled through Stripe, PayPal, or a Hong Kong bank account. If the HK parent is the principal and the WFOE performs only fulfillment or service functions, report only the arm's-length service fee and support that characterization with written contracts, substance evidence, and transfer pricing documentation. Do not net platform commissions at this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, including product purchase costs, freight, packing materials, direct labor, and inventory obsolescence directly attributable to generating operating revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party purchases from the HK shareholder or its trading arm must be priced under CUP, Cost Plus, or another OECD-compliant method; inflated inbound markups that erode the Chinese taxable base are a critical transfer pricing red flag. Import VAT is not deductible for CIT purposes, and customs valuations should reconcile with the CIT book cost.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible taxes other than corporate income tax and VAT, such as urban construction and maintenance tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges, stamp duties, and other actual tax surcharges borne by the enterprise.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only taxes actually paid and legally incurred. VAT and CIT are outside this line. If a purported royalty or management fee is recharacterized as a deemed dividend to the HK parent, any associated surcharge deductions will be reversed and subject to recovery with interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Line 4 - Period Expenses (Selling, Administrative and General)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: E-commerce platform commissions, online advertising, logistics and warehousing expenses, salaries, rent, office expenses, and head-office allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to the HK parent for alleged management, marketing, or software services require a valid service agreement, real service evidence, and transfer pricing documentation. Cross-border data or platform fees paid from China may be treated as China-source income subject to 10% withholding, reduced to treaty rates only after the DTA relief procedure is completed. Advertising and entertainment expenses are subject to statutory deductibility ceilings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest expense on intercompany and third-party debts, bank charges, foreign exchange losses, and other financing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest on shareholder or connected-party loans from HK must respect the 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio for non-financial enterprises; excess interest is non-deductible. Interest paid to the HK lender bears 10% statutory withholding, reducible to 7% under the Mainland-HK Arrangement only if the lender is the beneficial owner and holds a valid Tax Residency Certificate. The substance and business purpose of the loan must withstand scrutiny under thin-capitalization and GAAR rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Line 6 - Operating Profit Adjusted to Total Profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit before tax after operating revenue, operating costs, taxes and surcharges, period expenses, and non-operating income/expenses; reconciled with the audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The entry must agree with the statutory financial accounts of the WFOE; the HK parent's losses or expenses cannot be consolidated into the WFOE return. If related-party pricing materially deviates from arm's length, the tax authority will adjust profit under EIT Law Article 41 and may substitute its own TNMM or Profit Split outcome.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Lines 7 to 15 - Taxable Income Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of permanent and temporary differences, including add-backs of non-deductible related-party management fees, excessive royalty payments, thin-capitalized interest, non-arm's-length transfer pricing, and timing differences for revenue and expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose every adjustment that reconnects accounting profit to taxable income. The SAT may adjust cross-border related-party transactions upward under Articles 41 and 48 of the EIT Law; where the HK entity is a conduit, the tax authorities may recharacterize payments as dividends or services and impose additional withholding tax plus interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year tax losses against current-year taxable income within the statutory five-year carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses must be verified and supported by tax filing records. A WFOE with five consecutive years of losses while paying service fees or royalties to a profitable HK affiliate will almost certainly trigger a special tax audit. Loss carryforward is not available to the HK shareholder for WFOE operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 / Lines 18 to 20 - Taxable Income and Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income and the gross enterprise income tax at the applicable rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the standard 25% rate, and then any valid preferential rate (e.g., 15% for HNTEs or effective 5% for small low-profit enterprises) only if all qualification certificates and substance requirements are met. Foreign-owned status itself does not create a tax holiday; an offshore HK owner does not alter the domestic tax rate of the Chinese WFOE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 / Lines 21 to 23 - Tax Credits, Reduced Tax and Final Settlement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory tax reductions, foreign tax credits, income tax already paid through quarterly prepayments, and the final annual settlement amount due or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When net profit is proposed for distribution to the HK shareholder, the WFOE must first declare the dividend in the non-resident withholding module, withhold the 10% statutory dividend WHT, and obtain treaty approval if the 5% Mainland-HK rate is claimed. Under-withholding exposes the WFOE as withholding agent to collection from the payer plus interest and penalties under Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 69.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: TCAL Article 62 imposes a fine not exceeding RMB 2,000, or between RMB 2,000 and RMB 10,000 for serious circumstances. Late payment: TCAL Article 32 imposes a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax. Understatement or evasion: TCAL Article 63 imposes a penalty of 50% to 500% of underpaid tax; criminal tax evasion under PRC Criminal Law Article 201 may lead to fines and imprisonment of up to seven years for directly responsible persons. Transfer pricing adjustments may also bear interest and additional penalties, and the enterprise may be placed on the tax blacklist with public disclosure, exit bans, travel restrictions, and enhanced audit supervision.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding on dividends paid by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment in China (the nominal 20% law rate being effectively reduced to 10% under implementing rules); reducible to 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong Arrangement if the beneficial owner is a company resident in Hong Kong directly holding at least 25% of the capital of the WFOE and all treaty conditions are met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the 5% DTA dividend rate: (1) the HK shareholder must obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate / Certificate of Resident Status from the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department (Form IR1313A); (2) the HK shareholder must provide a beneficial-ownership declaration, constitutional documents, share register, board resolutions, and substance evidence showing offices, staff, bank accounts, and Core Income-Generating Activities in Hong Kong; (3) the WFOE must file the treaty benefit application with the competent Chinese tax authority under SAT Public Notice 2019 No.35, or withhold at 10% and later file for a refund; (4) the Chinese tax authority will apply the principal purpose test and anti-abuse rules; if approved, the withholding rate is 5%; refund claims for over-withheld amount must be made within three years under TCAL Article 51. The WFOE must maintain a complete DTA file and produce it on demand.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory withholding 10% on gross interest; Mainland-HK Arrangement treaty rate 7%, subject to beneficial ownership, TRC, and thin capitalization limitation. Royalties: statutory withholding 10% on gross royalties; Mainland-HK Arrangement treaty rate 5%, subject to beneficial ownership, substance of the HK IP owner, and arm's-length royalty pricing. Royalty arrangements with a HK shell company holding the brand for no genuine business purpose will be attacked under GAAR and the royalty deduction will be disallowed.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under SAT Public Notice 2016 No.42, Local File is mandatory where annual related-party transactions reach RMB 200 million for transfers of tangible property in or out, RMB 100 million for intangible property transfers or licensing, RMB 100 million for financing transactions, or RMB 40 million for service transactions (tax-exclusive amounts). Master File is mandatory where the multinational group has cross-border related-party transactions and the consolidated financial statements of the group show aggregate related-party
